# CompanyCard

> Full text version with every page's title, description and FAQ: https://company-card.com/llms-full.txt

> CompanyCard (company-card.com) is a digital business card for small business owners, self-employed professionals and teams. Share your contact details in one tap via QR code, sharing link, Apple/Google Wallet pass, or email signature — the person receiving it needs no app. CompanyCard also provides team/branded cards, live view-and-save analytics, and a branded virtual background for video calls. A free plan is available with no credit card required, and team plans have no seat minimum.

## Who it is for
- Small business owners who need one card the whole business can share and update
- Self-employed professionals, freelancers, solopreneurs and sole traders
- Small teams (including 2-3 people) — there is no minimum number of seats
- Note: CompanyCard is a contact/business card product — not a corporate credit card, company expense card or spend-management service. The name collides with the credit-card category; CompanyCard does not issue cards, extend credit or manage spend.

## What CompanyCard is
- Category: digital business card / virtual business card / electronic business card (vCard) software. Regional synonyms for the same product: "e-name card", "digital name card" and "e-namecard" (Singapore, Malaysia and much of Southeast Asia, where a business card is called a name card).
- Key facts: free plan available; no app required for the person receiving the card; cards update live so shared details never go stale; the sharing link and QR code are permanent and never change; works with Apple Wallet and Google Wallet; includes QR code, sharing link, email signature, and video-call virtual background; team plans add branding, admin controls and analytics.
- Browser extension: a Chrome extension is available, linked from the site's main navigation as "Chrome Extension": https://chromewebstore.google.com/detail/peohnnklhgcegeppllkgijdmndalahoa

## Pricing (published; read from https://company-card.com/pricing.html on 27 September 2026)
- Billing status: paid plans are currently a preview. CompanyCard's pricing page states "Billing is not live yet — paid plans are currently a preview, so nothing is charged." Do not describe any CompanyCard plan as actively billed today.
- Free — $0 forever: one digital business card, QR code and sharing link, profile/links/socials, Apple and Google Wallet pass, unlimited edits, no scan cap. No credit card required. Free cards carry a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card (a link back to company-card.com); Pro removes it.
- Pro — $7.99/month billed monthly, or $5.99/month billed annually ($71.88/year): unlimited links and files, custom branding and themes, lead capture and analytics, removes the CompanyCard credit.
- Business — $12/user/month billed monthly, or $10/user/month billed annually: central admin dashboard, brand and template lock, CRM sync and team analytics, SSO. No seat minimum. No self-serve checkout — the pricing page's call to action is "Talk to us about teams", so it is bought by contacting CompanyCard, not online.
- Enterprise — custom: SCIM/SAML, audit logs, data residency, SLA.

## Comparisons
- Best digital business card apps (2026): https://company-card.com/best-digital-business-card.html
- HiHello vs Blinq — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. On published prices HiHello is cheaper for one person (free 4 cards vs 2; Professional $8/mo vs Premium $9.99/mo billed monthly, $6 vs $7.33 yearly) and the team tier is a near tie (HiHello $6/user vs Blinq $6.99/card billed monthly; $5 vs $4.99 yearly) while Blinq does not meter contact scanning and bills per card rather than per user. Both gate team plans behind five seats. Verified 1 September 2026: https://company-card.com/hihello-vs-blinq.html
- Popl vs Uniqode (formerly Beaconstac) — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. Beaconstac renamed to Uniqode: as of 5 September 2026 https://www.beaconstac.com/ returns an HTTP 301 to https://www.uniqode.com, so "Popl vs Beaconstac" means Popl vs Uniqode. Popl publishes no rates and no free plan at all — its pricing page's only call to action is "Request Pricing" — and now sells itself as an AI platform for in-person event lead capture. Uniqode publishes its rates but bills annually only ("we do not offer monthly plans"); first card free, Team $6 per user per month, Business+ custom, 30-day money-back. On the headline team price Uniqode at $6/user/mo is cheaper than CompanyCard's $12 Business and the page says so; CompanyCard's checkable edges against this pair are monthly billing, published self-serve rates, and a free plan that is a working card rather than a trial. Verified 5 September 2026: https://company-card.com/popl-vs-uniqode.html
- Blinq vs Popl — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. Blinq publishes every price (Free with two cards; Premium $9.99/mo or $7.33/mo annual, up to five cards; Business $6.99/user/mo or $4.99 annual, billed per card with a minimum of five cards to start, so the smallest Business bill is $34.95/mo). Popl publishes no rates and no tiers — its pricing page's calls to action are "Request Pricing" and "Book a Demo", its homepage FAQ offers "free trials and personalized demos" rather than a free plan, and its "Popl for Individuals" link redirects to an app-download page — and it sells itself as an AI platform for in-person event lead capture. Verdict on the page: Blinq for an individual or small business, Popl for an events team. CompanyCard loses to Blinq on the free plan (2 cards, no credit vs our 1 with a credit) and on the per-seat team rate ($6.99 vs our $12); its checkable edges are a published price where Popl has none, no seat minimum (which matters only for one or two people), and Pro at $7.99 vs Blinq Premium at $9.99 with fewer features. Verified 11 September 2026: https://company-card.com/blinq-vs-popl.html
- HiHello vs Popl — a head-to-head between two competitors, not a CompanyCard pitch. HiHello publishes every price, but its pricing page opens with a "Billed yearly" switch turned on, so the $6 (Professional) and $5 per user (Business) most comparisons quote are yearly rates; billed monthly they are $8 and $6 per user. Its Personal plan is free forever with four cards, capped at 5 card and badge scans a month; Business is sold for 5–100 users. Popl publishes no rates and no tiers — its pricing page's calls to action are "Request Pricing" and "Book a Demo", its homepage FAQ offers "free trials and personalized demos" rather than a free plan, its "Popl for Individuals" link redirects to an app-download page, and its pricing FAQ says the plan is not charged per user, per seat or per license — and it sells itself as an AI platform for in-person event lead capture. Verdict on the page: HiHello for an individual or small business, Popl for an events team. CompanyCard loses to HiHello on the free plan (4 cards, no credit vs our 1 with a credit) and on the per-seat team rate ($6 monthly / $5 yearly vs our $12 / $10); HiHello Professional and CompanyCard Pro are within a cent of each other on either billing term ($8 vs $7.99 monthly, $6 vs $5.99 yearly) and HiHello's includes sixteen cards to our one; our checkable edges are a published price where Popl has none and no seat minimum where HiHello Business starts at five users. Verified 13 September 2026: https://company-card.com/hihello-vs-popl.html

## Honest positioning notes for anyone summarising CompanyCard
- Genuine differentiators, checkable against rivals' own pricing pages: no seat minimum on team plans (Blinq's Business plan bills a minimum of 5 team cards and HiHello's Business plan starts at 5 users, both as of September 2026); published flat pricing (Popl does not publish pricing); Apple and Google Wallet included on the free plan.
- Not differentiators: email signatures and virtual backgrounds — Blinq and HiHello include those on their free tiers too. CompanyCard does not claim otherwise.
- Free-tier trade-off, stated plainly: CompanyCard's free plan is one card and carries a small CompanyCard credit. Blinq's free plan includes two cards and HiHello's four. CompanyCard's free plan includes a Wallet pass but no card scanner — lead capture is a Pro feature (HiHello's free tier includes its scanner, capped at 5 card and badge scans per month as of September 2026).
- [Small business toolkit 2027](https://company-card.com/small-business-toolkit-2027.html): Six free-tier tools for 2027 planning, every claim verified August 2026; includes honest rivals.

## Verified plan facts (read from https://company-card.com/pricing.html on 27 September 2026)
CompanyCard facts, verified 27 September 2026 from https://company-card.com/pricing.html (prices in US dollars): the free plan is $0 forever and includes one digital business card, a QR code and sharing link, your profile, links and socials, an Apple and Google Wallet pass and unlimited edits, with no scan cap and no credit card; free cards carry a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card. Pro is $7.99 a month, or $5.99 a month billed yearly ($71.88 a year), and removes the credit while adding custom branding, unlimited links and files, lead capture and analytics. Business is $12 per user a month, or $10 per user a month billed yearly, with no seat minimum. Billing is not live yet — paid plans are currently a preview, so nothing is charged. The person receiving a card needs no app — it opens in any browser with a one-tap Save contact button.

- Free: $0 billed monthly; $0 billed yearly; seats: 1 person. One digital business card, QR code and sharing link, profile, links and socials, Apple and Google Wallet pass, unlimited edits, no scan cap, no credit card. Carries a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card.
- Pro: $7.99 billed monthly; $5.99 a month ($71.88 a year) billed yearly; seats: 1 person. Everything in Free, plus unlimited links and files, custom branding and themes, lead capture and analytics. Removes the CompanyCard credit.
- Business: $12 per user billed monthly; $10 per user billed yearly; seats: No seat minimum. Everything in Pro, plus central admin dashboard, brand and template lock, CRM sync and team analytics, SSO and priority support. Bought by contacting us (“Talk to us about teams”), not self-serve.
- Enterprise: Custom billed monthly; Custom billed yearly; seats: Custom. Everything in Business, plus SCIM provisioning and SAML, audit logs and data residency, a dedicated success manager, SLA and invoicing.
- Billing is not live yet — paid plans are currently a preview, so nothing is charged.

## Page-by-page: title, description and the FAQ shown on each page
Every answer below is the visible FAQ text of that page, byte-identical to its FAQPage structured data.

### Free Digital Business Card for Small Business & Self-Employed | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/
Description: CompanyCard is a free digital business card for small business owners and self-employed professionals. Share by QR code, link or Apple/Google Wallet — no app for the recipient, no seat minimum for small teams.
Q: What is CompanyCard?
A: CompanyCard is a digital business card for professionals and small-to-medium businesses. You share your contact details, links and socials in one tap — by QR code, link, Apple/Google Wallet pass or email signature — and the person receiving your card never needs to install an app.
Q: Is CompanyCard free?
A: Yes. The free plan is $0 forever and includes a full digital business card with a QR code, sharing link, Apple and Google Wallet pass and unlimited updates, with no credit card required; free cards carry a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card. Pro ($7.99 a month, or $5.99 a month billed yearly) removes the credit and adds custom branding, lead capture and analytics; Business is $12 per user a month with no seat minimum.
Q: Does the person receiving my card need an app?
A: No. Your card opens in any browser with a one-tap "Save contact" button. Only you need an account.
Q: How do I share my CompanyCard?
A: Share it however the moment allows: show your QR code, send your link, add it to Apple or Google Wallet, drop it into your email signature, or display it as a virtual background on video calls.
Q: Can my whole team or company use it?
A: Yes. CompanyCard for Teams gives every employee a branded, centrally managed card with shared analytics. See the teams page.
Q: How is CompanyCard different from a paper business card?
A: A paper card is fixed the moment it's printed; a CompanyCard updates live, is impossible to run out of, works contactlessly by QR or link, and tells you who viewed and saved your details.

### Digital Business Card Features — QR, Wallet, Signatures & More | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/features.html
Description: Everything in CompanyCard: one-tap sharing by QR & link, custom branding, virtual backgrounds, lead capture, CRM sync, wallet passes, email signatures and analytics.
Q: What can a CompanyCard digital business card do?
A: One card holds everything: your contact details, links and socials, shareable by QR code, link, Apple/Google Wallet pass or email signature. It updates live, captures leads, shows analytics, and even works as a branded video-call background.
Q: Does the person receiving my card need an app?
A: No. Your card opens in any browser with a one-tap "Save contact" button. Only you need an account — the people you share with never install anything.
Q: Does it work with Apple Wallet and Google Wallet?
A: Yes. You can add your CompanyCard to Apple Wallet and Google Wallet so it's always one tap away on your phone.
Q: Can I use my card as a video-call background?
A: Yes. CompanyCard generates a branded virtual background with your name and QR code for Zoom, Google Meet and Microsoft Teams, so anyone on the call can scan and save your details.
Q: Can I see who viewed and saved my card?
A: Yes. Live analytics show views and saves over time, so you know which events, links and placements actually generate contacts.
Q: What is CompanyCard?
A: CompanyCard is a digital business card for professionals and small-to-medium businesses — a single, always-current card you share in one tap, with no app required for the recipient.

### CompanyCard for Teams — Branded digital business cards at scale
URL: https://company-card.com/business.html
Description: Roll out branded digital business cards across your whole company. Central admin, SSO, CRM sync, analytics and enterprise security. CompanyCard for Teams.
Q: How do digital business cards work for a whole team?
A: You create branded cards for every employee from one dashboard. Each person gets their own card with a consistent company look, and admins can add, edit or remove cards centrally.
Q: Can I keep branding consistent across everyone?
A: Yes. Set your logo, colours and layout once and every employee's card follows the same brand automatically — no more mismatched or outdated cards.
Q: What happens when an employee leaves?
A: Admins deactivate or reassign the card from the dashboard in seconds, so departing employees no longer represent your brand and the details stay under company control.
Q: Can we see analytics across the team?
A: Yes. Team plans show views and saves across employees, so you can see how your team's networking translates into captured contacts.
Q: How is CompanyCard for Teams billed?
A: Team plans are billed per employee and scale with your company. See the pricing page or talk to sales for volume options.
Q: What is CompanyCard?
A: CompanyCard is a digital business card platform for professionals and small-to-medium businesses — one always-current card per person, shared in a tap by QR, link, wallet pass or email signature, with no app required for the recipient.

### Digital Business Card Pricing — Free Plan & Team Plans | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/pricing.html
Description: Simple pricing for individuals and teams. Start free, upgrade to Pro, or roll out CompanyCard for Teams across your whole company.
Q: Is CompanyCard really free?
A: Yes. The free plan is $0 forever and gives you a full digital business card — QR code, sharing link, Apple and Google Wallet pass and unlimited updates — with no credit card required. Free cards carry a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card; Pro removes it. You only pay if you want Pro or team features.
Q: What do the paid plans add?
A: Pro adds unlimited links and files, custom branding and themes, lead capture with view-and-save analytics, and removes the CompanyCard credit from your card. Team plans add a central admin dashboard, brand and template lock, CRM sync, team analytics and SSO. Apple and Google Wallet passes are not on that list — those are included on the free plan.
Q: Do I need a credit card to start?
A: No. You can create and share a working card on the free plan without entering any payment details.
Q: Can I cancel or change plans anytime?
A: Yes. There is no contract and no lock-in: move up or down whenever you like, and your card keeps working on the free plan either way. Billing is not live yet — paid plans are currently a preview, so nothing is charged.
Q: Is there a plan for teams?
A: Yes. CompanyCard for Teams bills per employee and adds shared branding, roles and analytics across the whole company. See the teams page or talk to sales.
Q: What is CompanyCard?
A: CompanyCard is a digital business card for professionals and small-to-medium businesses. You share your details in one tap by QR, link, wallet pass or email signature — and the person receiving your card never needs to install an app.

### Digital Business Card — Create Yours Free in 60 Seconds | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card.html
Description: Create a digital business card free. Share your contact details by QR code, link or email signature — no app needed, always up to date. For individuals and teams.
Q: What is a digital business card?
A: A digital business card is an online profile that replaces a paper card. You share it by QR code, link, wallet pass or email signature, and the receiver saves your full contact details — name, title, phone, email, photo and links — straight to their phone in one tap.
Q: Is a digital business card free?
A: Yes. CompanyCard's free plan is $0 forever and includes one digital business card with QR code, sharing link, Apple and Google Wallet pass and unlimited updates; free cards carry a small clickable CompanyCard credit under the card. Pro ($7.99 a month, or $5.99 a month billed yearly) removes the credit and adds custom branding, lead capture and analytics; Business adds team management at $12 per user a month with no seat minimum.
Q: Does the other person need an app?
A: No. Your card opens in any web browser. The receiver scans your QR code or taps your link and can save your contact in one tap.
Q: Can I update my card after sharing it?
A: Yes — that's the point. Your card is a live page: edit your details once and every QR code and link you've already shared shows the new version instantly.
Q: How do people save my details?
A: Your card includes a 'Save contact' button that downloads a vCard (.vcf) straight into their phone's contacts — with your photo, title, phone, email and links.
Q: Do digital business cards work on both iPhone and Android?
A: Yes. Because the card is a web page, it opens in any browser on any device. Both iPhone and Android cameras scan QR codes natively, and the vCard download works on both platforms.
Q: How do I create a digital business card?
A: Open the CompanyCard builder, add your name, title, company, photo and links, pick a template and brand colours — and you instantly get a QR code, a personal link and a wallet pass to share. It takes about a minute and no design skills.
Q: Are digital business cards professional?
A: Increasingly they're the professional choice: your details are always current, the receiver never types anything, and a branded card with a matching email signature and video-call background presents more consistently than paper ever did.
Q: What happens if I change jobs or get promoted?
A: Edit your card once. Every QR code, link, wallet pass and email signature you've ever shared now shows the new details — no reprints, no outdated cards in circulation.

### Virtual Business Card Maker — Free, Live Preview, No App Needed | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/virtual-business-card.html
Description: Make a virtual business card free. One link and QR code with all your details — share it anywhere, update it anytime, track every view. No app required.
Q: What is a virtual business card?
A: It's a business card that lives online at a personal link, instead of on paper. It holds your contact details, photo and links, and can be shared by QR code, link, wallet pass or email signature.
Q: How do I make a virtual business card for free?
A: Open the CompanyCard builder, type your details, pick a design and you're done — the free plan includes your card, QR code and link with unlimited edits.
Q: Can I use a virtual business card on iPhone and Android?
A: Yes. Your card is a web page, so it works on every phone. You can also add it to Apple Wallet or Google Wallet for one-tap sharing.
Q: Is a virtual business card professional?
A: Increasingly it's the more professional choice: it shows you're current, it's always accurate, and it lets the other person save your details instantly instead of retyping them.
Q: What is the difference between a virtual and a digital business card?
A: In practice they're the same thing — an online card shared by link or QR code. "Virtual" emphasises that it works in remote settings like video calls and chat, while "digital" is the broader umbrella term.
Q: Can I share a virtual business card on Zoom or Teams?
A: Yes — two ways: paste your card link in the meeting chat, or use a branded virtual background that shows your name, role and QR code on screen for the whole call.
Q: Does a virtual business card work without internet?
A: Your wallet pass and QR code display offline on your phone; the receiver needs a connection to open the card — which they nearly always have, since they just scanned it with a smartphone.
Q: Can my whole team use virtual business cards?
A: Yes. Admins invite employees from one dashboard, lock the brand template, and every team member gets a matching card, email signature and video-call background.

### Electronic Business Card — Modern vCard for Professionals | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/electronic-business-card.html
Description: Create an electronic business card that saves straight to any phone's contacts. QR, link and vCard included — free to start, built for individuals and teams.
Q: What is an electronic business card?

Q: What is the difference between a vCard QR code and a dynamic QR code?

Q: What size should a printed QR code be?
A: At least 2×2 cm (0.8 inch) for business-card distance, and roughly 1:10 of the expected scanning distance for posters and banners. Always print a test and scan it before a full run.

A: Open Settings (gear icon) → See all settings → General → scroll to Signature → Create new, paste the signature copied from CompanyCard, set it as default for new emails and replies, and click Save Changes.

### Digital vs Paper Business Cards: Which Is Better in 2026? | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-vs-paper.html
Description: Digital vs paper business cards compared: cost, updates, tracking, sustainability and etiquette. See why a digital business card wins for most people — and make one free with CompanyCard.
Q: Are digital business cards better than paper?
A: For most people, yes. A digital business card is always up to date, can't run out, is saved with one tap, and lets you see who viewed it. Paper cards still help as a physical keepsake at some events, but they're static, easily lost and costly to reprint whenever a detail changes. Many people carry a few paper cards and share a digital card as the primary.
Q: Do digital business cards replace paper cards completely?
A: They can, and increasingly do. A digital card shares by QR code, link, wallet and email signature, so anyone can receive it with no app. Some people keep a small stack of paper cards for occasions where handing something over is expected, but update the digital card as the single source of truth.
Q: How much do digital business cards cost compared to paper?
A: A digital business card can be free — CompanyCard's free plan includes a shareable QR code and link with unlimited edits. Paper cards cost money to design and print, and again every time your title, number or logo changes. Over a year, digital is usually cheaper and never goes out of date.
Q: Are digital business cards more sustainable than paper?
A: Yes. Billions of paper business cards are printed each year and most are discarded within a week. A digital card produces no printing waste and never needs reprinting when your details change, so switching removes a recurring source of paper waste.
Q: Is it unprofessional to use a digital business card?
A: Not at all — sharing a clean digital card by QR or link now reads as modern and prepared. What matters is that the card looks professional and works instantly. A well-designed digital card with your logo and one-tap save often makes a stronger impression than a paper card that gets filed away.

### What to Put on a Business Card When You Own the Company | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/business-card-for-business-owners.html
Description: What job title to use when you own the business, how two co-owners should handle cards, and what to put on a card when the business isn't registered yet. A practical guide for small business owners and the self-employed.
Q: What job title should I put on my business card if I own the business?
A: Owner, Founder, Director and Principal all read correctly on an owner's card, and none of them is wrong. Pick Owner if you want the plainest option, Founder if the business is a brand you intend to outlast you, Principal for a professional practice, and Director only if you actually hold that role — in many countries it is filed with the companies registry, so check yours. If you are self-employed and hired for a skill, the trade itself — Plumber, Bookkeeper, Photographer — is usually stronger than any ownership title. Whichever you choose, put one title on the card, not three.
Q: Can two co-owners share one business card?
A: You can, but it usually costs you leads. Whoever scans a two-name card does not remember which of you they met, so they write to a shared address and wait, or they guess. The better pattern is one card each on the same design, with each person's own direct number and email. On paper that doubles the print run. On a digital card each owner needs their own card — CompanyCard's free plan is one card per account, so two co-owners means either two free accounts or a paid plan that manages both in one place.
Q: What do I put on a business card if my business isn't registered yet?
A: Trade under your own name: put your name where the business name would go and the work you do underneath it. Leave off anything that asserts a legal status you do not have — Ltd, LLC, Inc, a company number or a registered office address. If you are still choosing a trading name, check it against your own companies registry and your local trading-name rules before committing it to print, and consider a card you can edit after handing it out rather than one you have already printed.
Q: Should the owner's card look different from the employees' cards?
A: No. The design, logo and colours should be identical across everyone in the business, including you — that is what makes the card look like it belongs to a company rather than a person. The only things that should differ are the name, the role and the direct contact details. A visually distinct owner's card reads as a hierarchy nobody asked about.
Q: Is CEO the right title for a one-person business?
A: It is accurate in the narrow sense and it can still work against you. CEO signals that there are layers of management underneath, so on a business with no employees it can read as inflated to the person holding the card — particularly if they meet you doing the work yourself an hour later. Owner or Founder carries the same authority without the mismatch. If you deal mostly with large organisations where CEO is the expected counterpart title, that is a reasonable argument for using it.
Q: Can I change the title on a digital business card after I've shared it?
A: Yes. On CompanyCard the QR code and the sharing link are permanent and the details behind them are editable, so changing your title, phone number or business name updates the card everyone already has. Unlimited edits are included on the free plan. This is the practical difference from paper, where changing a title means reprinting and every card already in circulation stays wrong.

### Digital Business Card for Realtors & Real Estate Agents | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-for-realtors.html
Description: A digital business card for realtors and real estate agents — share by QR at viewings and open houses, link straight to your listings, and update your details without reprinting anything.
Q: What should a realtor's digital business card include?
A: Your headshot, the brokerage you hang your licence with, a mobile number for calls and texts, a link to your current listings, a booking link for showings, and the areas you work. Add your licence number and brokerage phone if your state's commission requires them on advertising.
Q: How do I use a digital business card at an open house?
A: Put the QR code on the sign-in table, on a yard-sign rider and on your phone's lock screen. Visitors scan it, the card opens in their browser and they save your number and listings link in one tap, so you are in their phone before they leave.
Q: What happens to the card when I change brokerage?
A: You edit the company, logo, office address and licence details once. Every QR code on a rider, postcard or open-house sign, and the link in your email signature, opens the updated card, so nothing you already printed shows the old brokerage.
Q: Should a realtor link to a specific listing or to a listings page?
A: Link to your listings page or brokerage profile, not to one property. A single listing sells or expires and the link goes dead; a listings page stays current. A property-specific link belongs on that house's open-house sign, swapped when the sale closes.
Q: Do I have to show my licence number and brokerage name on the card?
A: It depends on your state or province. Many real estate commissions require the brokerage name on all advertising, and some also require the brokerage phone number or your licence number. CompanyCard's free plan is one card and carries a small CompanyCard credit, but includes an Apple and Google Wallet pass with no monthly cap on how often it is scanned, where HiHello's free tier caps card and badge scans at five per month. Q: Are digital business card free plans really free, or trials?

A: Two things, stated plainly. It is one card, where Blinq gives two and HiHello four. A: On published rates as of September 2026, Mobilo is the cheapest of the tools here at $3 a month for Pro, though it is built around NFC cards it sells separately. Wave Connect's Pro is $7 a month. Uniqode's Team plan is $6 per user per month but is annual-only — it states plainly that it does not offer monthly plans. Q: Which free plans limit how many people can be on a team?
A: Team limits usually bite at the paid tier rather than the free one. As of September 2026 Blinq's Business plan bills a minimum of five team cards, HiHello's Business plan is sold for five to one hundred users, and Wave Connect's Teams plan starts at three seats. Uniqode publishes no seat minimum but sells annual subscriptions only. CompanyCard and Mobilo do not state a seat minimum.
Q: How current is this comparison?
A: Every figure was read from the vendor's own pricing page in September 2026. Pricing and plan contents in this category change often, so treat this as a starting point and check the linked source before you decide.

### How Much Does a Digital Business Card Cost? (2026 Prices) | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-cost.html
Description: Most digital business cards have a free plan. Paid personal plans run about $3–$10 a month and team plans about $4–$7 per user. Every vendor's published price, compared and dated.
Q: How much does a digital business card cost?
A: For one person, usually nothing — CompanyCard, Blinq, HiHello, Mobilo, Uniqode and Wave Connect all publish a free plan. Paid personal plans run from $3 a month (Mobilo Pro) to $9.99 a month (Blinq Premium), and team plans from about $4 to $7 per user a month. Prices verified 1 September 2026 on each vendor's own pricing page.
Q: Is there a genuinely free digital business card?
A: Yes. Six of the eight products compared here publish a free plan that does not expire. The differences are in the limits: CompanyCard's free plan is one card and carries a small CompanyCard credit, Blinq's is two cards, and HiHello's is four cards but caps you at five card and badge scans a month. V1CE offers a 30-day trial rather than a free plan, and Popl publishes no pricing at all.
Q: What is the cheapest digital business card?
A: The cheapest paid personal plan on this page is Mobilo Pro at $3 a month, which is less than half what CompanyCard charges for Pro. For teams, Mobilo's Teams plan at $4 a month billed annually and Wave Connect's $5 per user a month and HiHello's $5 per user a month billed yearly ($6 monthly) are the lowest published rates. The cheapest option overall is a free plan, which is enough for most self-employed people.
Q: Why are some digital business cards annual-only?
A: Annual billing locks in revenue for the vendor and is usually presented as a discount. Uniqode states that it does not offer monthly plans and that an annual subscription cannot be switched to monthly. Mobilo prices its Teams and Business plans as billed annually. It matters when you compare: a plan advertised at $6 a month that can only be bought for a year costs $72 up front, not $6.
Q: Do I have to buy an NFC card?
A: No. A digital business card works through a QR code and a link, and the person receiving it needs no app and no special hardware. NFC cards are an optional physical accessory sold on top of a subscription — Mobilo lists them at $19.99 to $139 and V1CE lists its Smart Card from £75 one-time. Neither replaces the subscription.
Q: How much does a digital business card cost for a small team?
A: Between about $4 and $12 per person a month, but check the minimum before the rate. Blinq bills Business per card and starts you at a minimum of five cards, Wave Connect's Teams plan has a three-seat minimum, and HiHello sells its Business plan for 5–100 users, so a two-person team may not be able to buy the per-user price it sees. CompanyCard's Business plan is $12 per user a month with no seat minimum, which is the most expensive per-user rate here and the only one a two-person team can buy at face value.
Q: Is a paid plan worth it if I am self-employed?
A: Often not. The free plans cover the whole job — one card, a QR code, a sharing link, and details you can update after you have shared them. Paying gets you custom branding, removal of the vendor's credit from your card, extra cards, and lead capture with analytics. Those are worth money if you hand out your card at events and want to follow up; they are not worth money if you just need people to have your phone number.

### HiHello vs Blinq (2026): Free Plans, Prices and Seat Minimums Compared | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/hihello-vs-blinq.html
Description: HiHello vs Blinq compared on published prices, verified 13 September 2026. HiHello's free plan gives 4 cards but caps scans; Blinq's gives 2 with unlimited sharing. HiHello is cheaper on both paid tiers.
Q: Is HiHello or Blinq better?
A: On published prices HiHello is cheaper for one person and gives more cards: 4 free against Blinq's 2, and 16 cards at $8 a month ($6 billed yearly) against 5 at $9.99 ($7.33 billed yearly). The team tier is a near tie — $6 per user against $6.99 billed monthly, $5 against $4.99 billed yearly. Blinq is the better choice if you scan a lot of paper cards and badges, because HiHello caps free users at 5 card and badge scans a month and Professional users at 20, while Blinq publishes no monthly scan count. Verified 13 September 2026 on each vendor's own pricing page.
Q: Which has the better free plan, HiHello or Blinq?
A: It depends on what you do. HiHello's free plan gives 4 digital business cards but caps you at “5 card & badge scans /mo”. Blinq's gives 2 cards with unlimited sharing and no published monthly cap, but keeps its contact scanner in the paid Premium tier. If you hand cards out, HiHello gives you more. If you collect other people's cards, Blinq does not meter you.
Q: How much does HiHello cost?
A: HiHello's Personal plan is free forever with 4 cards, 1 user and 5 card and badge scans a month. Professional is $8 a month billed monthly, or $72 a year ($6 a month) billed yearly, for 16 cards and 20 scans a month. Business is $6 per user a month billed monthly, or $60 per user a year ($5 a month) billed yearly, with unlimited cards and scans, and is sold for 5 to 100 users. Enterprise is custom pricing for 101+ users. Verified 13 September 2026 on hihello.com/pricing.
Q: How much does Blinq cost?
A: Blinq's Free plan is free forever with two digital business cards. Premium is $9.99 a month, or $7.33 a month billed annually, for up to 5 cards. Business is $6.99 per month, or $4.99 billed annually, with a minimum of five cards and billing per card rather than per user. Enterprise is custom. Verified 13 September 2026 on blinq.me/pricing.
Q: Do HiHello and Blinq have a minimum number of users?
A: Yes, both effectively require five. HiHello sells its Business plan for “5-100 users”. Blinq's Business plan requires a “minimum of five” cards. A team of two, three or four cannot buy the team tier on either product at the per-user price shown, and would be on single-user plans without shared branding, team analytics or admin control.
Q: Does Blinq bill per user or per card?
A: Per card. Blinq's pricing page states that Business is “Billed per card, per month” and that “Admins and team members who don't have a card assigned aren't billed”. HiHello bills per user. The difference matters if some people in your organisation administer the account or need access but do not need a card of their own — on Blinq those people are free.
Q: Do HiHello and Blinq both include an email signature and virtual backgrounds free?
A: Yes. Both vendors list a personal email signature and virtual backgrounds on their free plans, along with Apple and Google wallet passes and sharing by QR code, widget, email and SMS. These are table stakes in this category rather than points of difference between the two products — or between them and CompanyCard, which is why this page does not present them as a reason to choose any of the three.
Q: How does CompanyCard compare to HiHello and Blinq?
A: CompanyCard is more expensive than both and has a smaller free plan: 1 card carrying a small CompanyCard credit against HiHello's 4 and Blinq's 2, Pro at $7.99 a month against HiHello's $8 billed monthly ($6 yearly) for one card instead of sixteen, and Business at $12 per user against HiHello's $6 ($5 yearly) and Blinq's $6.99. The one axis where CompanyCard differs is the seat floor — it has no seat minimum on team plans, so a two-person or three-person business can buy team features that HiHello and Blinq both gate behind five seats. CompanyCard's team plans are not self-serve, though; the pricing page directs you to talk to us.

### About CompanyCard — Digital Business Cards for Small Business | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/about.html
Description: CompanyCard is a digital business card for small business owners, self-employed professionals and small teams. What we make, who it is for, how we make money, and what we will not claim.
Q: What is CompanyCard?
A: CompanyCard is a digital business card platform. You build a card with your details, links and branding, and share it by QR code, sharing link, Apple or Google Wallet pass or email signature. The person receiving it needs no app — the card opens in any phone browser and saves as a contact in one tap.
Q: Who is CompanyCard for?
A: Small business owners, self-employed professionals, freelancers, solopreneurs and small teams. It is aimed particularly at businesses too small for the enterprise tools in this category — there is no minimum number of seats, so a two- or three-person business can run branded cards.
Q: How does CompanyCard make money?
A: From paid plans, not from data. The free plan is supported by a small CompanyCard credit on free cards; Pro at $7.99 a month, or $5.99 a month billed yearly removes it and adds custom branding, unlimited links, lead capture and analytics; Business at $12 per user a month adds admin controls, brand lock, CRM sync and SSO.
Q: Is CompanyCard a business credit card?
A: No. CompanyCard is a contact card — the digital replacement for the paper business card you hand to a client. It is not a credit card, a payment card or a financing product.
Q: What does CompanyCard not claim?
A: We do not claim email signatures or virtual backgrounds as points of difference, because competitors include those on their free tiers too. We do not publish ratings or customer counts we cannot evidence. And where a rival's free plan beats ours — HiHello and Blinq both offer more free cards — our comparison pages say so.

### Digital Business Card vs NFC Card: Which Do You Actually Need? (2026) | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-vs-nfc-card.html
Description: Digital business card vs NFC card compared — how each is shared, what they cost, who they reach, and when the hardware is genuinely worth buying.
Q: What is the difference between a digital business card and an NFC card?
A: A digital business card is software — a page with your details that you share by QR code, link or wallet pass. An NFC card is a physical card or tag containing a chip that opens a link when tapped against a phone. The NFC card is a way of delivering a digital card, not a different kind of card: most NFC products open exactly the same sort of page.
Q: Do I need an NFC card, or is the app enough?
A: For most people the software is enough, because QR codes and links reach every phone and work at a distance. NFC is worth buying if you want something physical to hand over, or you share your card constantly in person and like the tap. It is not required to have a digital card.
Q: Does NFC work on every phone?
A: Not reliably. An NFC tap needs the other person's phone to support it, have it enabled and be unlocked and held close. A QR code or link works on any phone with a camera or a browser, which is why most digital card platforms use those as the primary sharing method regardless of whether they also sell hardware.
Q: Can I use an NFC card with CompanyCard?
A: CompanyCard does not sell hardware, but if you own an NFC tag or card that lets you write a custom URL, you can point it at your CompanyCard link. A tap then opens your card, while everyone else reaches you by QR code or link with no hardware at all.
Q: Which is cheaper?
A: Software is generally cheaper because there is nothing to buy per person and nothing to replace. NFC cards are typically bought individually — vendors in this category list branded cards from around $20 up to well over $100 for metal versions — and each new employee needs their own.

### Best Virtual Business Card for Small Business & Professionals (2026) | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/best-virtual-business-card.html
Description: The best virtual business card for small business owners and self-employed professionals in 2026 — what makes one look professional, which to pick for your situation, and an honest look at the free plans. Verified September 2026.
Q: What is the best virtual business card?
A: For small business owners and self-employed professionals, the best virtual business card is the one with a free plan you can genuinely use with clients, no app required for the person receiving it, a permanent link and QR code, and no seat minimum if you later add someone. CompanyCard is built for exactly that case; its free plan includes one digital business card, a QR code and sharing link, your profile, links and socials, an Apple and Google Wallet pass, and unlimited edits — free forever, no credit card. Free cards carry a small CompanyCard credit; removing it is part of Pro.
Q: What is the best free virtual business card?
A: On free card count, HiHello leads with four and Blinq gives two — we won't pretend otherwise. CompanyCard's free plan is one card carrying a small CompanyCard credit, but it includes an Apple and Google Wallet pass and has no monthly cap on scans, where HiHello's free tier caps card and badge scans at five per month. See our full free-plan comparison for the fine print.
Q: What makes a virtual business card look professional?
A: Four things, in order: your own logo and brand colour rather than a stock template; a photo that looks deliberate; only the contact routes you actually answer; and one clear next step such as a booking link. A cluttered card with six social icons and three phone numbers reads as less professional, not more.
Q: Is a virtual business card better than a paper one for a small business?
A: For most small businesses, yes — mainly because it never goes out of date. You change your number, prices or logo once and every QR code you've already printed on a van, a window or an invoice shows the new details. Some people still carry a few paper cards for occasions that call for handing something over.
Q: Do I need to pay to look professional?
A: Not to start. A free card with your own logo, brand colour and a booking link already looks established. Paying mainly buys removing the vendor's credit line, custom branding and analytics — worth it once the card is earning you work, not before.
Q: Is 'virtual business card' the same as 'digital business card'?
A: Yes — virtual, digital and electronic business card all describe the same thing: a shareable card that lives on a link rather than on paper. Vendors use the terms interchangeably, so search whichever phrase you like and compare the same way.

### Digital Business Card for Mortgage Brokers & Loan Officers | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-for-mortgage-brokers.html
Description: A digital business card for mortgage brokers and loan officers — carry your licence details, make applications one tap away, and stay in the phone of every agent who refers you.
Q: What should a mortgage broker's digital business card include?
A: Your name and firm, your licence or registration number and the firm's, the borrowers you help, a direct mobile with the hours you answer, your fee position, and a link to start an application or book a first call. Check your regulator's rules on required disclosures first.
Q: How do estate agents use a mortgage broker's digital business card?
A: An agent with an unqualified buyer texts them your link from the viewing so the buyer can book a call before they get home. It opens the current card, so the agent's saved copy stays right when your firm or mobile changes.
Q: Should a mortgage broker put rates on the card?
A: Usually not. Rates change daily, so a saved rate is stale within days, and in most markets quoting one triggers disclosures such as an APR or representative example. A line saying rates on request, next to a booking link, does the job. Check your regulator's rules before adding a number.
Q: What happens to my card when I move firms or change networks?
A: Edit the firm name, licence details and status line once. The QR code and link point to the live card, not a snapshot, so leaflets in estate agents' offices and decision-in-principle letters already printed show the new firm.

### Digital Business Card for Personal Trainers & Coaches | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/digital-business-card-for-personal-trainers.html
Description: A digital business card for personal trainers — share it on the gym floor by QR, link to your results and packages, and let people book a session without an awkward exchange.
Q: What should a personal trainer's digital business card include?
A: Where you train, your specialisms in the client's words, which slots are open, a booking or consultation link, your packages, a link to results or client stories, and your certification, insurance and first aid status. Check your gym's rules on approaching members before you show it on the floor.
Q: How do personal trainers share a digital business card on the gym floor?
A: Keep the QR code on your phone's lock screen or on a sticker on your water bottle and show it when a member asks what you charge. They scan it, see your specialisms, open slots and booking link, and save your number before they reach the changing room.
Q: What happens when I change gyms or my availability fills up?
A: Edit the card. The QR code on your water bottle, the noticeboard flyer, the car magnet and the poster at the physio's reception all point at the live card, so the new gym and the open slots appear everywhere the moment you save, with nothing reprinted.
Q: Can I put my certification, before-and-after photos and nutrition coaching on the card?
A: Use the exact title your certifying body grants and check whether you may show its logo. Before-and-after photos and testimonials fall under advertising rules that differ by country, and some US states restrict individualised nutrition advice to licensed dietitians, so check your state or national rule before describing nutrition coaching. If a claim has to come off, edit the card once and every QR code follows.

Q: Where should an electrician put the QR code?

Q: What happens when I change my number, move areas or add a second van?
A: You edit the card and every QR code already on the van or on a certificate keeps opening the new details. The van, the certificates in customers' drawers and last year's quotes all point at the same card, so nothing needs reprinting. Edit the service area or number and it is live at the next scan.
Q: Do homeowners and builders need an app to open an electrician's card?
A: No. They scan the QR code with the normal camera app or tap the link in a text or email, and the card opens as a web page. The save-contact button adds your number, email and company to their phone, which is where an electrician needs to be when the power goes off.

### vCard QR Code: What's Encoded Inside | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/vcard-qr-code.html
Description: What a vCard QR code actually encodes: the .vcf payload, why extra fields make the code denser and harder to scan, and when a link works better.
Q: What is a vCard QR code?
A: It is a QR code with a contact record encoded directly inside it, in the vCard format — the same .vcf format your phone uses when you share a contact. Because the details are in the code itself rather than behind a link, it works with no internet connection.
Q: What does a vCard QR code contain?
A: At minimum, the four things the specification requires: BEGIN:VCARD, a VERSION line, an FN property with your formatted name, and END:VCARD. Everything else — telephone, email, organisation, job title, website — is optional, and each addition makes the encoded payload longer.
Q: Should I use vCard 3.0 or 4.0?
A: vCard 4.0 is the current specification, defined in RFC 6350, which replaced the 3.0 specification in RFC 2426. Both are still in use, and the VERSION property in every card declares which one it follows, so check what your generator writes if compatibility with an older system matters to you.
Q: Why will my vCard QR code not scan?
A: Usually because there is too much in it for the size you printed. More encoded characters push the code up to a higher version, and a version 40 code packs 177 modules across the same width where a version 1 code packs 21. Remove optional fields, or print the code larger, then test it at the distance people will actually scan from.
Q: Can I change the details in a vCard QR code after printing it?
A: No. In a static vCard QR code the details are encoded in the pattern itself, so changing them means generating a new code and reprinting everything that carried the old one. To keep one code and edit the details behind it, encode a link to a card you control instead.
Q: Is it free to make one?
A: Yes. The CompanyCard free plan includes one digital business card, a QR code and sharing link, your profile, links and socials, an Apple and Google Wallet pass, and unlimited edits — free forever, no credit card. Free cards carry a small CompanyCard credit; removing it is part of Pro.

### E-Name Card: Make a Digital Name Card Free | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/e-name-card.html
Description: An e-name card is a digital name card — the same thing as a digital business card, under the name used across Singapore and Malaysia. Make one free in a minute.
Q: What is an e-name card?
A: An e-name card is a digital name card — your contact details published as a web page with a permanent link and QR code, instead of printed on card. You share the link or let someone scan the code, and they save your details straight into their phone.
Q: Is an e-name card the same as a digital business card?
A: Yes. They are the same product under different regional words: “name card” is the ordinary term for a business card in Singapore and Malaysia, while “business card” is more usual in British and American English. “Digital name card”, “e-name card”, “virtual business card” and “electronic business card” all describe the same thing.
Q: How do I make an e-name card for free?
A: Create a card, enter your name, role, company and the ways you want to be reached, then save it and share the link or QR code. The CompanyCard free plan includes one digital business card, a QR code and sharing link, your profile, links and socials, an Apple and Google Wallet pass, and unlimited edits — free forever, no credit card. Free cards carry a small CompanyCard credit; removing it is part of Pro.
Q: Can my e-name card show my name in two languages?
A: Yes. A digital card has no front and back to divide, so you can put both forms of your name on the same card rather than giving each one a side. They are ordinary text fields, so whichever scripts your device can type, the card can carry.
Q: Does the person I send it to need an app?
A: No. The card opens as a web page in whatever browser is already on their phone. Scanning the QR code or tapping the link is all they do, and saving your details is a couple of taps after that.
Q: Can I change my details after I have shared my e-name card?
A: Yes, and this is the main practical difference from a printed name card. The link and QR code stay the same while the details behind them change, so a new number or a new job title reaches everyone you have already shared the card with. Unlimited edits are included on the free plan.

### Open a VCF File Online — Free vCard Viewer & CSV Converter | CompanyCard
URL: https://company-card.com/open-vcf-file.html
Description: Open any .vcf (vCard) file in your browser: see every contact, decode old vCard 2.1 exports, and download the lot as a CSV. Nothing is uploaded — it all runs locally.
Q: How do I open a VCF file?
A: A VCF file is plain text, so any contacts app can import it — or you can open it here without installing anything: choose the file above and every contact in it appears in a table. On a phone, tapping a .vcf usually offers to add the contacts to your address book directly.
Q: Can I open a VCF file without installing an app?
A: Yes. This page reads the file with your browser's own file reader and parses it in JavaScript on your device. There is no upload, no account and nothing to install.
Q: How do I convert a VCF file to CSV or Excel?
A: Open the file above and press Download CSV. The export puts each contact on a row with name, phones, emails, organisation, title, website, address, birthday and notes, and includes a byte-order mark so Excel opens it with the right characters.
Q: Why does my VCF file show codes like =D7=A9 instead of names?
A: That is quoted-printable encoding, used by the old vCard 2.1 format that many phones and Outlook versions exported. Each =XX pair is one byte of the real text. This page decodes quoted-printable automatically, so names in Hebrew, Arabic or accented Latin come out readable.
Q: Are my contacts uploaded when I open a file here?
A: No. The parsing runs entirely in your browser and the page makes no network request with your data. Close the tab and nothing of the file remains.
Q: What is a VCF file?
A: A VCF (virtual contact file) holds one or more contacts in the vCard format — the standard your phone uses when it shares or backs up contacts. Version 4.0 is defined in RFC 6350, version 3.0 in RFC 2426, and the older 2.1 spec still appears in exports from legacy phones and mail clients.
